title: Shelf Search

scenario.intro: The vault's search desk hands back every item on every shelf, in no order at all.
scenario.goal: Ask the database for items up to `max_price`, cheapest first, with a `?` parameter.

objective: The desk lists only what you can afford, cheapest first.
rules: Pass `max_price` as a `?` parameter, never inside the SQL string.

hints.text: SQL reads like a sentence: SELECT what FROM where WHERE condition ORDER BY column.
Put a ? in the SQL where the value goes, and pass the values as a tuple: db.execute(sql, (max_price,)). The comma makes it a tuple.
Something like: "SELECT name FROM items WHERE price <= ? ORDER BY price", (max_price,)

dialogue.start: Every shelf at once? Nobody can find anything like this.
dialogue.success: Neat rows, cheapest first. Just how I like my shelves.
dialogue.fail: Some items are out of budget or out of order.
